description: Make the data layer filter-aware. Change fetchCommandCenter to accept a CommandCenterFilter and apply the resolved period per module using the CORRECT date column for each table, keep every safeSelect defensive, keep it admin-only, and include the filter in the query key so TanStack Query caches per-filter. Decide and implement which tiles respect the range vs stay point-in-time, matching the documented model. Depends on FEAT-002.
steps: Change the signature to fetchCommandCenter(filter: CommandCenterFilter) and commandCenterQuery(filter: CommandCenterFilter). Default behavior when the caller passes period 'all' must equal today's all-time numbers (backward-compatible baseline). Resolve the window once at the top: const period = resolvePeriod(filter.period, { from: filter.from, to: filter.to }). Use period.fromISO/toISO for timestamptz columns and period.fromDate/toDate for plain `date` columns.

Update the queryKey to ['admin-command-center', filter.period, filter.from ?? null, filter.to ?? null, filter.day ?? null] (as const) so changing any filter refetches and caches independently. Keep staleTime 60s.

Sales + Business Overview (leads.created_at is timestamptz; bookings has booking_date `date` and created_at timestamptz): add .gte/.lte on leads.created_at using fromISO/toISO, and on bookings use booking_date with fromDate/toDate (booking_date is the business-meaningful date, consistent with the bookings page filter). When period is 'all', skip the bounds (or rely on the 1970 lower bound) so results match current all-time behavior. Keep the ROW_LIMIT and safeSelect wrappers.

B2B modules: filter b2b_leads by created_at (timestamptz, fromISO/toISO), b2b_activities by happened_at, referrals by COALESCE semantics — the row carries referral_date, date_received, created_at; filter in SQL on the primary date column (referral_date) with .gte/.lte on fromDate/toDate, and because a row may only have date_received/created_at, do the authoritative range check in a pure helper after fetch using inRangeDate/inRangeISO on the best available date, so no referral is wrongly dropped. b2b_followups: filter by due_at within the window for the overdue computation input, but preserve the existing overdue-vs-now semantics in activityBreakdown (overdue is still measured against real now, not the window). Keep buildFunnel/activityBreakdown/employeeLeaderboard/topPartners fed from the now-range-scoped row sets.

POINT-IN-TIME tiles that must NOT change with the range (document this): 'Active CA Partners' and 'Partners' (ca_firms.partner_status is a current-state snapshot), 'Open Pipeline' (current open-lead count), and the overdue-follow-ups count (measured vs real now). Keep these computed from unfiltered current-state reads (or from the full firm/lead set) regardless of the selected period. Add a short comment at each explaining why.

Renewals (bookings.plan_expiry_date / renewal_followup_at): renewals are a forward-looking current-state view (due/pending/completed/dormant relative to now). Keep this block point-in-time relative to real now; do NOT scope it to an arbitrary past range (a past window would make 'due' meaningless). Add a comment documenting this choice.

Documentation (documentation_tasks.created_at timestamptz): scope the fetched tasks to the window via created_at .gte/.lte (fromISO/toISO). docSummary already takes a `now` for TAT math; keep passing real now for TAT breach cutoff, but the counted task set respects the window. Document that 'completed/pending/delayed' then reflect tasks CREATED in the window while TAT is still measured against now.

Attendance (attendance.work_date `date`): drive this block by the DAY filter, not the period range. If filter.day is set, use that single YYYY-MM-DD for the work_date gte/lte and for the approved-leave overlap; otherwise fall back to today's date via the existing local-date helper. Rename the hardcoded todayRange() usage to a dayRange(day?: string) that defaults to today, built from LOCAL date parts (not toISOString slicing, to avoid UTC drift — fix the existing start.toISOString().slice bug while here by composing YYYY-MM-DD from getFullYear/getMonth/getDate). Return the resolved attendance day so the UI can label it.

Payroll (salary_slips.month, a YYYY-MM-01 key): payroll runs monthly. Interpret the filter as: if filter.day or the period resolves to a single month, use that month's key; otherwise default to the current month (unchanged behavior). Simplest correct rule: derive the month key from period.toDate (the end of the selected window) when a period is selected, else current month. Keep this clearly labeled as a monthly view. Document the choice.

Return the same CommandCenterData shape plus a small meta describing the resolved window and attendance day (e.g. add `meta: { periodLabel: string, fromDate: string, toDate: string, attendanceDay: string }`) so the UI can show accurate labels. Keep all existing fields intact and types exported.

Create src/lib/command-center-queries.test.ts ONLY IF a pure, extractable mapping/helper is introduced here (e.g. the referral best-date selection or the month-key derivation). If such a helper is added, export it and cover it with concrete-value tests. Do not attempt to unit-test the Supabase-coupled fetch itself (the pure maths it calls are already covered); prefer extracting any non-trivial logic into command-center.ts and testing it there.
acceptance_criteria: fetchCommandCenter(filter) and commandCenterQuery(filter) compile and the queryKey includes period/from/to/day so distinct filters cache separately.

Each module filters on its correct date column: leads.created_at, bookings.booking_date, documentation_tasks.created_at, b2b_leads.created_at, b2b_activities.happened_at, referrals via referral_date/date_received/created_at best-date, attendance.work_date (driven by the Day filter), salary_slips.month (monthly).

Point-in-time tiles (Active CA Partners/Partners, Open Pipeline, Renewals block, overdue follow-ups) remain computed against current state / real now and do NOT shift with the period range, with an explaining comment at each.
Passing period 'all' with no day yields numbers equal to the pre-change all-time dashboard (backward-compatible), and the Attendance block with no day still shows today.
Every read remains wrapped in safeSelect (returns [] on error, never throws); the module stays admin-only (no change to the dashboard.tsx gating).
The returned data includes a meta block with periodLabel/fromDate/toDate/attendanceDay for UI labeling.
The pre-existing UTC-slice bug in the attendance day range is replaced with local-date-parts composition.
`./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit` passes and any extracted helper has concrete-value tests that pass.
findings: Made the command-center data layer filter-aware. fetchCommandCenter(filter) and commandCenterQuery(filter) now accept a CommandCenterFilter; commandCenterQuery defaults to { period: 'all' } so the existing FEAT-004-pending call site in admin-command-center.tsx still compiles and reproduces the all-time dashboard (no component change needed here). queryKey is now ['admin-command-center', period, from??null, to??null, day??null] as const, staleTime kept at 60s. Resolved the window once via resolvePeriod. Per-module date columns: leads.created_at (fromISO/toISO), bookings.booking_date (fromDate/toDate), b2b_leads.created_at, b2b_activities.happened_at, documentation_tasks.created_at (fromISO/toISO), b2b_followups.due_at used as the fetch window. Referrals: lenient fetch + authoritative JS range check via inRangeDate(bestReferralDate(r), fromDate, toDate) so rows carrying only date_received/created_at are not dropped. POINT-IN-TIME (unfiltered vs real now, each with an explaining comment): Open Pipeline (re-read from unfiltered leads and overwritten on sales.pipelineOpen), Active CA Partners / total Partners (ca_firms.partner_status snapshot), overdue follow-ups (recomputed from an UNFILTERED pending-followups read against real now, overriding the range-scoped activity.overdueFollowups), and the whole Renewals block. Documentation counts respect the created-at window while docSummary still receives real now for TAT. Attendance is driven by filter.day with a today fallback; replaced todayRange() (which had the start.toISOString().slice UTC-drift bug) with dayRange(day?) built from LOCAL getFullYear/getMonth/getDate. Payroll stays monthly; monthKey derived from monthKeyFromDate(period.toDate) falling back to the current month. Added meta: { periodLabel, fromDate, toDate, attendanceDay } to CommandCenterData. Extracted two pure helpers into command-center.ts (bestReferralDate, monthKeyFromDate) and added concrete-value tests in command-center.test.ts (5 new cases). Verification green: ./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit (0), bun run test (261 passed, up from 256), bun run build (ok). No change to dashboard.tsx gating; all reads remain safeSelect-wrapped. V1-REVIEW FIX (issue #1, backward-compat edge for 'all'): under period 'all' the ranged reads previously applied resolvePeriod's upper bound (end-of-today), which dropped legitimately future-dated bookings.booking_date rows that the pre-change unbounded dashboard counted. Fixed by SCOPING the fix to the query layer (command-center-queries.ts) rather than changing resolvePeriod's 'all' toDate to a 9999 sentinel. Rationale: resolvePeriod is SHARED with the sales-performance page (src/routes/_authenticated/admin/sales-performance.tsx renders a caption directly from `period.fromDate -> period.toDate`) and the b2b analytics filter bar (src/components/b2b/analytics-shared.tsx); both now render an 'All time' button because PERIOD_OPTIONS gained 'all' in FEAT-002, so a far-future toDate ('9999-12-31') would surface a misleading '1970-01-01 -> 9999-12-31' caption there. Query-layer scoping is lower risk and leaves those callers untouched. Implementation: added a withWindow(q, column, from, to, unbounded) helper that applies .gte/.lte only when NOT unbounded, plus an isAll = filter.period === 'all' flag; every ranged read (leads.created_at, bookings.booking_date, b2b_leads.created_at, b2b_activities.happened_at, b2b_followups.due_at, documentation_tasks.created_at) now skips both bounds under 'all', and the referral JS range filter is skipped under 'all' too so every (incl. future-dated) referral is kept. Payroll month-key is UNCHANGED and still correct: resolvePeriod was not touched, so period.toDate for 'all' remains end-of-today and monthKeyFromDate(period.toDate) resolves Payroll to the CURRENT month (no 9999 month, no special-case needed). Added an explanatory comment to the 'all' assertion in report-period.test.ts documenting that the truly-unbounded behavior lives in the query layer. Re-ran the full gate after the fix: tsc --noEmit (0), bun run test (261 passed), bun run build (ok).
